newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan oil product stocks seen lowering throughput.
newsitem.headline: Japan oil product stocks seen lowering throughput.

text.p: Heavy oil product stocks could force Japanese oil companies to reduce refinery operating rates and possibly increase exports in the months ahead, oil industry sources say.
"There's a good chance that crude runs will be cut -- certainly they aren't likely to rise," a trader with a leading oil refiner said.
Most industry sources say oil product stock levels will be the primary factor to determine whether to cut throughput.
Latest government data shows that Japanese oil refineries' utilisation rate stood at 70.6 percent in May compared with 67.8 percent in the same month last year and 69.9 percent in May 1995.

The same data, provided by the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI), shows that year-on-year stockpiles of gas oil and kerosene have made double-digit percentage rate gains since the beginning of the year.
May gas oil stocks, the only exception to the double digit growth, grew by 9.6 percent from May 1996.
End-May gas oil stocks amounted to 2.2 million kl.
Kerosene stocks amounted to 3.1 million kl at the end of May, up 47.1 percent from a year earlier and up 12.9 percent from April.

MITI and some oil industry officials attributed the year-on-year jumps partly to the maintenance of low stockpiles last year, a policy which was widely believed to have been taken to try to tighten up the market ahead of industry deregulation in April 1996.
MITI said that this year's oil product stocks are only slightly higher than in an average year.

A Trade Ministry official said that inventory rates -- a key indicator calculated by dividing stockpiles by sales figures -- stood at 2.45 percent in May compared to 1.48 percent in the same month in 1996.
He said last month's rate was slightly higher than the 10-year average of 2.14 percent.
But oil traders said that markets were sensing a glut.

A trader at one company said its oil product trading unit had stepped up exports of middle-distillate to China and gasoline blending component to the United States in response to the high stock levels.
A total of 361,000 kl of gas oil were exported from Japan last month, up 85.1 percent from May 1996 and up 129.9 percent from April.
"Exporting provides one alternative in trying to trim stock levels," an industry source said.
He said Japanese companies would look at the oil products market both at home and in Singapore when making the decision.
A weak market in Singapore would keep the stocks at home, he said.
Industry sources said lacklustre refinery margins were also likely to play a role in determining operating rates.
One trader said current refinery margins of roughly $2 dollars per barrel, compared to levels of $4 to $5 per barrel during more profitable periods, were likely to worsen in July.
"I can't see the (domestic oil products) market rebounding so sharply in the short term," he said.
